label: The intelligible species is that by which the human intellect understands
summary: I q.85 a.2 distinguishes the species as the means of human knowing from the object known. The species is a candidate witness for Intelligible f and HasForm x f in the human case. The claim that it is the means of this cognition adds information beyond those two predicates.
blocker: The intelligible species is a candidate witness for both Intelligible f and HasForm x f in the human case. Show that each modeled instance of understanding admits such a witness, preserving the identity of intellect and species in the divine self-understanding case. Identifying f as the means of the particular cognition is additional interpretation beyond what the target’s existential requires.
